core_obligations: Identify the dualizing complex of the proper scheme as omega_X[d] and deduce that omega_X is a dualizing module (proof lines 7123-7127).
Transfer Cohen-Macaulayness from X to omega_X and deduce the four stated properties (proof lines 7127-7131).
proof_roadmap: The Cohen-Macaulay property and the inherited duality statements (proof lines 7127-7131).
difficulty_reason: Let X be a proper scheme over a field k which is Cohen-Macaulay and equidimensional of dimension d, and let omega_X be the module extracted from the dualizing complex of Lemma labelled lemma-duality-proper-over-field (statement lines 7105-7121). The lemma asserts four things: that omega_X is a dualizing module, that it is a coherent Cohen-Macaulay module with support all of X, that Ext^i_X(K, omega_X[d]) is Hom_k(H^{-i}(X, K), k) functorially in K in D_QCoh(X) and compatible with shifts and distinguished triangles, and that Ext^{d-i}(F, omega_X) is Hom_k(H^i(X, F), k) for quasi-coherent F. The proof identifies the dualizing complex as omega_X[d], where omega_X is the leftmost nonvanishing cohomology sheaf, so that omega_X is a dualizing module, and then uses Lemma labelled lemma-dualizing-module-CM-scheme to see that omega_X is Cohen-Macaulay because X is (proof lines 7123-7131). The remaining duality pairings are read off from the corresponding statements of Lemma labelled lemma-duality-proper-over-field. Recognizing omega_X^bullet as omega_X[d] and transferring the Cohen-Macaulay property from X to omega_X is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.
